D65·kd7r — 2026-10-12
rule: The test gate never forces a test run by default; holding the Stop until tests pass is a strict mode the operator turns on.
operator: "By default it will not need to be forced, right? That is the best UX and if the user really wanted a strict kind of thing, then they can turn on that"
chose: Felt-latency L1: the Stop test gate gets a per-clone mode, `advise` by default. An ask (rule-bearing edits with no covering pass after the last edit) never holds a Stop on its own. It rides the write-back hold when that fires anyway, returns in the sofar_end_session result as an in-band ask, and otherwise reaches the operator as a non-blocking systemMessage. A failed covering run still holds once, as memory-lead D37 rules, because no test run is forced there. `sofar check --strict-tests on` (or SOFAR_TEST_GATE=hold) restores the every-turn hold; drive sessions run `hold`; SOFAR_ENFORCE=off stays the off arm.
over: Keeping r3-fixes D10/D11's every-turn ask-hold as the default: 78% of 547 holds in 14 days, held turns 17.6% of active time, full-suite asks p50 22 s. Gate off by default: loses r3-fixes D11's catch of 9 of 13 regressing sessions. Background test runs: sofar would execute commands at every Stop, which r3-fixes D10 rejected at up to 45 s a turn and needing operator approval.
because: Operator P9 asked for no forced tests by default with strict opt-in, and P11 for faster without compromise. The in-band ask keeps the catch at the moment the agent declares done.
